stage: Stage 14: Suggested qty follows the chosen supplier
note: 1.13 is a numbers release. A /cart line under a supplier other than its item's usual (effective) one gets a suggestion of its own, rebuilt on that supplier's lead (cart.ts supplierSuggestion: a window minimum re-derived as the stored monthly burn x that lead / 30.44, a hand-set minimum unchanged, no minimum weekly x that lead / 7; an unknown or the same lead keeps the item's own). Where such a line shows its suggestion (no typed or carried qty) its qty and estCost follow, and with them its supplier's subtotal, the header ends, the quantity the decisions and pick-conflict lists repeat, the in-cart compare option's qty, and that line's Order qty and Est cost in cart.csv (plus its supplier's block heading, a cart.csv note). A typed line's suggestedQty moves, never its qty. A rebuilt line's rationale names its own lead (leadTimeDaysUsed, leadTimeUsedFor, leadTimeUsedSource, leadStock, rawNeed, leadTimeWeeks, leadTimeSource). Additive everywhere: qtyTyped and rationale.suggestionFor on every line, suggestedQty, suggestedEstCost and suggestionBasis on every option. Nothing else may move: every item's own suggestion, items, item pages, lines under the usual supplier, lead times, costs, states, cards, both other CSVs. The wildcards below would let a quantity move on any line, so the record-level proof is `stage-check qty <before> <after>`: the lines that moved equal the lines predicted from <before>, each to the predicted figure, typed quantities did not move, the totals add up from the lines, cart.csv moved only on predicted rows, and every other /cart field is identical.
